a pragmatic recruitment strategy and online screening process can be used to recruit and screen men at high risk for TDM.

a pragmatic recruitment and online self-screening process was effective in recruiting and selecting men at high risk for type 2 diabetes, that the intervention was appealing, and that the intervention was acceptable and had high overall satisfaction.
the pragmatic recruitment process was effective in recruiting men to a weight loss program for T2DM risk reduction, and that the intervention was acceptable and engaging for men.

the development of an intervention to help people with diabetes to manage their condition.
the evaluation of the effectiveness of a lifestyle intervention for men at high risk for TDM.
the design of a new type of intervention, a gender-targeted, lifestyle-based intervention for the prevention of T2DM in men.

the PULSE program was acceptable to men at high risk for type 2 diabetes.

the process evaluation of the T2D PULSE Program Randomised Controlled Trial was effective in determining the effectiveness of recruitment and acceptability of a gender-targeted lifestyle intervention.
the PULSE Program was an effective and acceptable intervention for men at risk of T2D.

we were able to recruit a high number of men who were at risk for developing T2DM.
men are willing to engage in weight loss and T2DM prevention programs, and that a gender-targeted intervention can be delivered effectively using self-administration.
